name: Khmer pinpeat royal-court ensemble
lineage: Khmer pinpeat ceremonial ensemble — the largest classical Cambodian instrumental tradition, accompanying the Royal Ballet of Cambodia and Sbek Thom shadow-puppet. Pre-Angkor Khmer roots; royal court and wat temple ceremonial repertoire. Canonical instrumentation of nine-to-ten instruments dominated by wind and percussion: roneat ek high bamboo xylophone (twenty-one bars, boat-shaped resonator, melodic lead), roneat thung low bamboo xylophone (second voice, counterpoint to ek), sralai quadruple-reed conical-bore oboe (palm-leaf reed, sustained melodic lead), sampho double-headed barrel timekeeper drum (sets tempo and cadence — ensemble leader), skor thom large barrel drum pair (stick-struck bass), kong vong thom large gong circle (sixteen tuned bronze bossed gongs in rattan frame — melodic skeleton sustaining the harmonic foundation), ching small finger cymbals (time-keeping). Seven-equal-tempered tuning shared with Thai piphat. The Khmer Rouge era 1975-1979 nearly destroyed the tradition; post-1980 reconstruction led by surviving masters including Chum Ngek, with the Royal University of Fine Arts Phnom Penh restoring transmission infrastructure. Distinguished from Thai piphat by Khmer-language repertoire and dialect-specific cadential conventions; distinguished from Lao seb-noi by the larger pinpeat ensemble configuration and royal-court ceremonial repertoire base
